subject: API contract grandfathering & phased endpoint consolidation plan
content:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: API contract grandfathering & phased endpoint consolidation plan

Folks —

Quick background: we need a short, cross-functional alignment on how we handle customers currently on the legacy /v1 endpoints as we consolidate to the new consolidated endpoint surface. ACME (external) signaled yesterday they expect a formal grandfathering window and explicit SLA language in the event we flip routing.

Asks:
- Product: confirm the recommended grandfathering window (months) and whether feature flags or aliases will fully cover behavior differences.
- Infra/Serving: outline the fallback criteria and any hard cutover constraints (max parallel variants we can support).
- Sales/CS: list top-5 customers who will need an explicit carveout and the commercial asks (credits, extended support).

Attached: draft "grandfathering_matrix.xlsx" and a short "comm_plan_draft.md" to help shape customer messaging.

I'm aiming to publish an official plan to customers by EOD Monday. Please reply with concrete delta items by 3pm PT today so I can synthesize.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Sean — quick take from Product:
- Recommendation: 6 month grandfathering window as default, with the option for 9 months on a case-by-case (commercial) basis. 6 months gives customers time to migrate without blocking our deprecation schedule.
- Compatibility: we should offer a compatibility alias that routes to the new model but enforces legacy tokenization/response framing for parity. That'll handle ~80% of differences. Remaining behavioral deltas should be documented and surfaced as "known diffs".
- Guardrails: we will allow per-customer feature flags for up to 12 months, but they will count against the maximum variant budget.

I'll attach a short matrix of behaviors in the attached spreadsheet. Need confirmation from Ben that we can hold those variants concurrently.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. PM, Model Serving

----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 13:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API contract grandfathering & phased endpoint consolidation plan

Marissa / team —

Short answer: we can support the compatibility alias and per-customer feature flags, but there are non-trivial constraints:
- Variant budget: cluster capacity and routing table complexity mean we can reliably support ~15 active compatibility variants in parallel per region before latency/regression risk increases.
- Autoscaler: the autoscaler needs predictable traffic patterns; large carveouts (several high-TPS customers) require reserved-capacity or dedicated lanes.
- Cutover safety: hard cutover should include a staged traffic shift (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on 5xx/latency/regression thresholds. We cannot perform more than two major canary waves concurrently on the same model family.

Operational asks:
- Provide list of customers with estimated RPS and peak windows so we can model capacity cost.
- If legal/commercial require an SLA amendment for extended grandfathering, update infra early so we can size reserved capacity.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: API contract grandfathering & phased endpoint consolidation plan

Looping in the commercial perspective — ACME flagged that their procurement needs a 9-month explicit carveout in contract language, plus an option for a single 6-month extension tied to feature parity milestones. They also asked about migration support (two joint migration sprints with our Solutions team).

Practical asks from Sales:
- If we commit to 9 months for ACME, we should attach clear exit criteria (e.g., compatibility alias coverage + migration runbook) and a modest credit for operational overhead.
- Need a concise customer-facing FAQ that outlines the steps and their responsibilities so CS can run a migration playbook.

I copied Andy (ACME) so we can avoid surprises; Andy, if you have specific RPS numbers for peak windows please share.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales

Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API contract grandfathering & phased endpoint consolidation plan

Thanks team — good signal.

Decision and next steps:
1) Approve a default 6-month grandfathering window. Exceptions (e.g., ACME) can be approved up to 9 months by Sales + VP nod with explicit exit criteria.
2) Product to finalize the compatibility-alias plan and a "known diffs" doc; infra to confirm variant budget and provide a simple runbook for staged cutover and rollback thresholds.
3) Sales/CS to produce customer migration FAQ and mark named customers that will need dedicated capacity. Provide RPS estimates by COB tomorrow so infra can model.
4) Sean: synthesize a customer communication template and publish it to the docs link below; include the credit language only after legal has reviewed.

I'll hold any exception approvals until I see the migration runbook and cost model. If anything looks risky from a reliability or cost standpoint, we will require reserved capacity commitments.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
